summary: Ten ideas targeting completely uncovered content pillars — social commerce, AI content quality, GEO measurement, live shopping, co-marketing, and AI maturity — with the four highest-priority angles anchored in real GSC striking-distance signals and rising 2026 trends. (2 idea(s) descartada(s): 1 por repetir algo ya propuesto o escrito, 1 por pisarse con otro título.)

competitors: Jasper has fully pivoted to enterprise with its 2026 State of AI in Marketing report (1,400-marketer survey, financial-services governance content, 'AI maturity as ROI predictor' research) — abandoning SMB editorial almost entirely and leaving a wide-open lane for anyone who speaks directly to owners and small teams.

Writesonic is aggressively owning GEO measurement space ('7 GEO KPIs Every Brand Must Measure,' 'GEO Action Center,' '10 GEO Platforms Tested') but writes exclusively for agencies and enterprise brands — every piece assumes a $500+/month tool budget, locking out the entire SMB segment.

HubSpot dominates broad 'AI for small business' with mega-listicles (27 tools, 35 tools, State of Marketing 2026 with 1,500 marketers) but provides almost no implementation depth — their content answers 'what' and rarely 'how in two hours with $50/month,' which is where SMBs actually need help.

Copy.ai shifted its editorial focus from copywriting features to GTM workflow automation and sales processes; their November 10, 2026 'AI Slop: Avoiding Low-Quality AI Content' post signals a new quality-vs-quantity content angle that no SMB-focused publication has picked up yet — a first-mover gap.
trends: Social commerce crossed $2.11T globally in 2026 (up from $1.63T in 2025); TikTok Shop delivers a 4.7% in-app conversion rate vs Instagram Shopping's 2.1%, and TikTok LIVE now accounts for 14% of TikTok Shop GMV — making live selling the most underexploited SMB growth channel of the year.

Agentic AI for SMBs moved from hype to operational reality: autonomous workflows managing lead response, content scheduling, and customer support are available at $20–$150/month, allowing two-person teams to run marketing operations that previously required a five-person agency retainer.

AI content quality ('AI slop') is now a recognized brand risk — 91% of marketing teams use AI (Jasper 2026 State of AI data) but content saturation is triggering audience trust erosion; brands that demonstrate human-in-the-loop editorial standards are gaining measurable authority advantages in both organic and AI search.

GEO/AEO measurement is the missing layer in AI search strategy: brands have invested in optimization but lack SMB-appropriate KPIs to prove ROI — Writesonic and Peec AI (€89/month, top pick for under-10-person teams) are defining the enterprise stack while the sub-$200/month measurement gap remains entirely unserved.

AI avatar and AI clone content is emerging as the bridge between faceless-brand scale and personal-brand trust — described as the highest-converting faceless content format in 2026, letting solopreneurs and tiny teams produce relationship-level video without filming overhead or personal exposure.
